Per-vendor consent with click-to-load embeds

Prototype for #545 (map #537). Four ways to ask before a YouTube, TikTok or Bluesky embed loads, on one “Talked about now” row with real titles from this week (Other Mommy, Animals, The Social Reckoning, The Odyssey, East of Eden) and the real players behind the facades. Built 14 October 2026.

Recommendation

C as the base, with D's question for the start-page row. Both keep the site free of a banner, cost about 4 KB only where embeds are, and ask at the moment the visitor wants the video, which is the most specific consent of the four. One store (consent_embeds, per vendor) serves both: the row asks once with D's chips, a title page's facade asks itself with C's “Remember for …”. B costs five times the code, puts 15.5 KB on every first view, and its “Always allow” loads every embed of a vendor at once. A only earns its banner if the analytics question (below) is settled in the same step.

Read this first

  • There is no analytics consent today. <CookieConsent /> is commented out in both places in root.tsx, and nothing reads cookie_consent. PostHog (localStorage+cookie), Google Analytics and Sentry load for every visitor without asking. A and B turn the dormant yes/no into a real opt-in, which drops analytics for everyone who declines; C and D leave it exactly as it is.
  • TikTok's player asks for its own cookies inside the iframe (“Allow cookies from TikTok on this browser?”), seen from this German connection. Every variant gets that second prompt after its own; GoodWatch cannot remove it.
  • No embed vendor is contacted before consent in any variant: the facades use GoodWatch's TMDB artwork and inline logos, and each variant's panel lists every vendor host the page has reached (checked at first visit, desktop and phone).
  • vanilla-cookieconsent hides itself from automated browsers by default (hideFromBots); the prototype turns that off so the screenshots show it.

Run it

Branch ghostex/6fb57e30. In goodwatch-webapp of a worktree on that branch, without a .env (the route needs no services):

npm ci && npx patch-package
REC_TASTE_MATCH=on REC_FILTER_BAR=on REC_WATCH_NEXT=on REC_TASTE_PAGE=on REC_EXPLORER=on REC_NAVIGATION=on REC_AGE_FILTER=on REC_TRACKING=on npx remix vite:dev --port 3145

Then open http://localhost:3145/prototype/consent; ?variant=A|B|C|D, or the arrows on the pill and the ← → keys. Each variant keeps its own stored consent; “Reset & reload” in the purple panel starts it over.

A Extend CookieConsent

Tests: Does the current banner, extended with a toggle per vendor beside Analytics, plus a facade that asks for its vendor when clicked, feel like enough?

Tradeoffs: Familiar and cheap (≈4.8 KB gzip own code), and the only way here to also settle analytics consent. But it brings a banner back to every landing page, and a first-time visitor needs three clicks to the first video (dismiss, play, allow).

localhost:3145/prototype/consent?variant=A

Desktop, 1280 px

Phone, 390 px

B vanilla-cookieconsent v3 + iframemanager

Tests: Do the two libraries, wired as their own demo wires them and themed dark, beat writing it ourselves?

Tradeoffs: Most complete preferences UI for no design work, but ≈23.6 KB gzip (15.5 KB of it on every page's first view), facade notices we can only restyle, two clicks to play even after “Load once”, and “Always allow” mounts every embed of that vendor on the page at once.

localhost:3145/prototype/consent?variant=B

Desktop, 1280 px

Phone, 390 px

C Facade only

Tests: Is the click on a facade that says where the video comes from enough consent, with a “Remember for YouTube” checkbox instead of any banner?

Tradeoffs: One click to the first video, ≈3.9 KB gzip only where embeds are, nothing site-wide. The facade carries more text (host, IP, privacy link, checkbox), and analytics stay as they are today.

localhost:3145/prototype/consent?variant=C

Desktop, 1280 px

Phone, 390 px

D Ask in the row (added)

Tests: Should consent belong to the “Talked about now” row: one question with a chip per source, no site banner and no question per card?

Tradeoffs: One decision for the whole row, Bluesky posts then show by themselves and videos play on one click; a source left off offers itself on its card. ≈4.3 KB gzip only where the row is. Until answered the row is only GoodWatch's artwork and words; analytics stay as today.
